summary: The candidate is correct as stated. The smallest admissible case k=3 gives R=8, n=6, W=7/2, and Lambda_0=2, consistently with all claimed bounds. The binary-layer construction has exactly the stated lattice points; extremality gives the outer fibers exactly, and midpoint inclusion together with the common simplex containment gives the central fiber exactly. Full dimension and rationality follow from the stated spanning and vertex arguments. Each noncentral reflected pair is counted once in the canonical measure, so its mass is exactly kRw+V, while the reflected overlap is W=V+2kRw. For every point in the central simplex, a maximal barycentric coordinate yields a proper closed halfspace disjoint from all but one midpoint component, including boundary points. This proves the upper bound Rw+V, and Rw>=V gives 2Lambda_0/(k+1). Both integer-dimension estimates hold for every k>=3. The n=0 specialization of predecessor 6d6fcf377e68c79c applies to the nonzero finite Borel measure kappa_0 and gives the lower bound Lambda_0/k. The concluding failure of an absolute normalized fixed-center bound has the correct quantifiers and does not assert a counterexample to the joint mixed-integer centerpoint problem.
